def test_is_sorted():
    # Sorted lists with no element appearing more than twice
    assert is_sorted([1, 2, 3]) == True
    assert is_sorted([1, 2, 2, 3]) == True
    assert is_sorted([1, 1, 2]) == True
    assert is_sorted([5]) == True
    assert is_sorted([]) == True
    assert is_sorted([1, 1]) == True

    # Sorted but an element appears more than twice
    assert is_sorted([1, 2, 2, 2, 3]) == False
    assert is_sorted([1, 1, 1]) == False
    assert is_sorted([2, 2, 2, 3, 4]) == False

    # Not sorted
    assert is_sorted([3, 2, 1]) == False
    assert is_sorted([1, 3, 2]) == False
    assert is_sorted([5, 4, 3, 2, 1]) == False
    assert is_sorted([2, 1]) == False

    # Duplicates plus unsorted
    assert is_sorted([1, 2, 2, 1]) == False

    # Negative numbers and mixed values
    assert is_sorted([-3, -2, -1, 0]) == True
    assert is_sorted([-1, -1, 0, 1]) == True
    assert is_sorted([-1, -1, -1, 0]) == False
    assert is_sorted([0, -1, 1]) == False

    # Non-integer values (works with comparables)
    assert is_sorted(['a', 'b', 'c']) == True
    assert is_sorted(['b', 'a']) == False
    assert is_sorted([1.5, 2.5, 2.5]) == True
    assert is_sorted([1.5, 2.5, 2.5, 2.5]) == False

    print("All tests passed!")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    test_is_sorted()
